learn.title: Evaluating
learn.body: To evaluate an expression, replace each variable with its value, then follow the order of operations. This is called substitution. Use brackets around a negative value so the sign stays attached.

learn.title: Like terms
learn.body: Like terms have the same variable part. $4x$ and $3x$ are like terms, and you can add them: $4x+3x=7x$. Terms like $4x$ and $3$ are not alike, so they stay separate. Think of $x$ as an apple: 4 apples and 3 apples make 7 apples.

learn.title: Simplify $5a+2-2a+7$
learn.body: Group the like terms, then combine them.
To check a simplified expression, try a number. With $a=2$, both $5a+2-2a+7$ and $3a+9$ give 15.

questions.explanation: $(-3)^2=9$, because a negative times a negative is positive. Then $9+1=10$.
The terms are alike, so add the coefficients: $4+3=7$.

questions.prompt: Which expression cannot be simplified further?
questions.explanation: $4x$ and $3$ are not like terms. The others combine into $7x$ and $5x$.

questions.prompt: Evaluate $2x+3$ when $x=-1$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Replace the variable, follow the order of operations, and keep the sign.
